_comment: Cookie Run OvenBreak — auto Send-Life to friends (Friends tab, home screen). Precondition: sit on home with the Friends tab already selected (default tab) so the leaderboard/friends list with per-row Send-Life icons is visible. Loop: scan for any visible green Send-Life icon -> tap it -> confirm the 'Send <name> a free Life?' dialog -> confirm the 'Message sent!' popup -> back to scan. When no icon is visible, swipe the list up to reveal more rows and re-scan; if still nothing after the swipe, the list is exhausted -> stop. SPEED-TUNED 2026-08-18 (second pass): poll_ms 250 and the hot-path waits trimmed again — scan 450, confirm 450, message_sent 400, scroll 800. Measured from the 2026-08-15/16 run (1411s, 164 sends, 0 close_popup retries across the whole pass): 84% of the wall clock sat in the three per-send states, and their cost was poll + tap + settle + the close_popup verify grab, not the taps themselves. The verify re-detect is KEPT everywhere — it is the fix for 'the close sometimes does not take' and it never once had to retry at these timings, which is the evidence the settle waits were oversized rather than load-bearing. Cold-path settles (peel_* 1000, probe_inactive 4000, recover_* 4000/12000, guard_not_partyrun 1200) are untouched: they fire a handful of times per run, so trimming them buys nothing and each covers a slower animation or a login round-trip. All coords verified live @1920x1080.

scan._note: Look for ANY visible Send-Life icon (green pill, heart+mail glyph) among the currently rendered rows — matchTemplate finds whichever instance scores highest, so it doesn't matter which row. Already-sent rows show a green CHECK instead (different glyph, won't match). Tap it via tap_template so we hit the icon wherever it sits on screen.

peel_popups._note: No Send-Life icon visible — before deciding the list is exhausted, rule out a popup covering it. Cookie Run drops modals at any time, not just at launch (Daily Check-in, Power+ Treasure Rewards, Congratulations/level-up rewards, friend-info), and any of them hides the friends list. Each popup peels to its own confirm and the list is still underneath, so we return to scan (not home). This is a mini modal chain: dailycheckin(OK 965,985) -> treasure(Confirm 960,850) -> congrats(Confirm 954,847) -> levelup(Confirm 954,847). None present -> genuinely no icon on screen -> scroll_list. Shared templates/coords with boxrun_default.json.

peel_treasure._note: Power+ Treasure Rewards popup. Confirm (960,850) -> scan. Absent -> peel_congrats.

peel_congrats._note: Congratulations! / reward popup (also covers level-up rewards — same green Confirm button). Confirm (954,847) -> scan. Absent -> no popup at all -> scroll_list to look for more rows.

confirm_dialog._note: Send-Life confirm dialog, NEW format "Send <name> a free Life?" (no Gift Points line). Detect the name-agnostic "a free Life?" text (self=1.000). Tap Confirm (1189,687 — green/right); NEVER Cancel. Absent -> confirm_dialog_gp checks the OLD format "...(+3 Gift Points)" before giving up, so both dialog versions are handled (the game dropped the Gift Points line in a patch; older accounts/regions may still show it).

confirm_dialog_gp._note: Send-Life confirm dialog, OLD format with the "(+3 Gift Points)" line (sendlife_confirm_gp_marker). Same Confirm coord (1189,687). Present -> tap Confirm -> message_sent. Absent -> neither dialog format is up (a stray double-match, or it already closed) -> message_sent/scan so we never get stuck.

message_sent._note: 'Message sent!' confirmation popup. Tap its Confirm (957,685) to close, returning to the friends list with that row now showing a green check instead of the send icon. Then back to scan for the next one.

scroll_list._note: No Send-Life icon visible in the current viewport — either all visible rows are already sent/checked/OFF, or we've scrolled past them. Swipe the list up (reveal lower rows) then re-scan. A run of consecutive already-handled rows (checks + gift-OFF friends) can span MANY screens back to back, so a single swipe-and-recheck is not enough evidence of bottom-of-list -> chain into scroll_retry, which keeps swiping (up to 6 total attempts) before concluding we're truly at the bottom. Each swipe is a fresh attempt, so a long OFF-streak just costs a few extra swipes instead of a false stop.

scroll_retry_1._note: Recheck after swipe #1. Found -> resume scanning. Still absent -> swipe again (attempt #2) rather than giving up — long OFF/checked streaks need several swipes to clear.

scroll_retry_4._note: Swipe attempt #5. If this and the next both miss, a swipe is producing no further list movement (the list itself has stopped scrolling, not just a long OFF-streak) -> genuinely at the bottom.

scroll_retry_5._note: Swipe attempt #6 (final). Still nothing after 6 consecutive swipes -> the list has stopped moving -> bottom of the friends list reached -> stop. EXIT FIXED 2026-08-19: stopping here left the Friends panel over home — see exit_to_home for what that cost.

exit_to_home._note:
Leaves the Friends panel before handing control back. The panel has no X: Android BACK closes it, which is how a human does it. detect is home_marker, so each step is a wait-for-home rather than a tap-and-hope — on_match means home is really there and the errand can end. Three bounded attempts rather than a self-loop: pressing BACK on home itself raises the game's own 'Exit the game?' dialog, so this must never press it forever. ADDED 2026-08-19: scroll_retry_5 used to `stop` outright, ending the errand with the panel still over home. The caller then switches Episodes, and switch_episode taps the Episode button at (1280,175) straight into the panel — caught live 09:02-09:05: Episode 1 finished, all six switches failed with 'Episode Map did not open', the restore failed too, and the farm loop ran against an Episode nobody chose until the watchdog fired at 1100s.

MARKER FIXED 2026-08-20: this waited on home/home_marker.png, which has the words "Episode 1" cropped inside it — measured against a real home frame with Episode 2 selected it scores 0.431 (absent) while home/home_play_marker.png scores 1.000. Live that day, three cycles running, Send-Life reached Episodes 1 and 2 and then failed every switch to 3-7 with "Episode Map did not open", plus the restore of the original Episode: on Episode 1 this chain matched and stopped with 0 BACK presses and the next switch worked on the first tap; on Episode 2 it matched nothing, pressed BACK three times, and handed control back on whatever screen that left. The farm configs moved to the Play! marker earlier (see coinrun.json on why the Episode-banner marker "silently broke"); these errands were missed.

exit_to_home_2._note:
Second BACK press — see exit_to_home.

exit_to_home_3._note:
Third and last BACK press — see exit_to_home. Hands the result of its own BACK press to exit_to_home_verify instead of stopping on it unchecked. The old note claimed the caller re-reads the Episode and refuses to switch blind — it does not: _run_errand_per_episode reads the Episode once, before the loop, and switch_episode's own home guard uses the Play! marker, which matched while this chain's episode-bound one did not. So an unchecked stop here was exactly the blind switch the note said could not happen.

exit_dismiss_exitgame._note:
Clears the game's own "Exit the game?" dialog, which this chain's own BACK presses raise: the first BACK closes the Friends panel and lands on home, and every press after that is a BACK on home, which is what opens it (exit_to_home says so in its note — nothing acted on it until now). Snapped live 2026-08-20 09:13:55 on the frame where "Episode Map did not open" fired: the dialog was centred over home while home/home_play_marker.png still scored 1.000 through it (Play! is bottom-right, the dialog is centred, nothing overlaps), so switch_episode's wait-for-home guard passed and it tapped the Episode button into the modal three times. Episodes 3-7 failed that way three cycles running, and the restore of the original Episode with them.

Cancel at (727,685), NEVER Confirm at (1188,684) — Confirm closes the game. Both centres measured off that frame by colour blob (grey pill vs green pill). close_popup rather than a bare tap so the marker clearing is verified; absent means some other BACK already took it away.

exit_to_home_verify._note:
Final look after the third BACK. Reached only when home was not seen after three presses, which before 2026-08-20 meant the chain stopped on an unknown screen and the caller tapped the Episode button into it (Episodes 3-7 all failed "Episode Map did not open", three cycles running). Home here -> stop clean. Still not home -> stop anyway, because a fourth BACK on home raises the game's own "Exit the game?" dialog and pressing more is how that gets hit; the difference is that the caller's own home guard now decides, and this state's absent branch is the one log line that says the exit chain gave up.

Reached after exit_dismiss_exitgame 2026-08-20, so "still not home" here means the Exit dialog was not what was in the way — a genuinely unknown screen. Stopping is still right: the caller's switch_episode has its own home guard and refuses to switch when it cannot see home, and this state's absent branch is the log line that says the exit chain gave up.

probe_inactive._note: Home-side inactive guard. 'You've been inactive for a while. The game will restart!' can queue on/over home after a long idle. Confirm (953,690) lets the restart proceed, then hand to recover_login to re-auth. Absent -> probe_prevresults.

recover_login._note: Login recovery step 1 (DevPlay title). After the inactive-restart the game reopens on the DevPlay title with the orange 'DevPlay Login' button (devplaylogin_marker, self=1.0). Present -> tap it (960,950) to open the account picker, wait for the fade, hand to recover_pick. Absent -> we may already be at the picker (or past login) -> recover_pick.

recover_pick._note: Login recovery step 2 (account picker). login_marker = 'You already have an account!' + CookieRun logo (name-agnostic). Present -> tap the top saved account row (1100,490), wait out the ~12s login + home load, re-enter start_state (scan). Absent -> the picker isn't up (login already completed, or the title is still animating) -> go to start_state and let its own detection settle; if we're still on the title, home will be absent and the probe chain loops us back to recover_login.

guard_not_partyrun._note: Close Party Run's 'Select a Mode' screen (added 2026-08-06, same guard the bot configs carry). This errand runs on the home screen with the full template tree, so Party Run is reachable here for the same reason it was there: a tap in the top-right banner strip opens it, nothing else in this config can detect it, and every state then misses while the chain keeps transitioning — a log that reads healthy while nothing progresses. close_popup (not a bare tap) so a close that does not take says so in the log: the blind-tap version of this guard sat on Party Run for 38 passes in silence. partyrun_marker.png scores 1.000 on that screen and <=0.403 on every other captured frame, so the 0.85 threshold this config uses is as safe as the bots' 0.82.

recover_unknown._note:
Watchdog recovery entry (src/fsm.py no_progress_goto), mirroring the bot configs. Reached when no progress state has been touched for no_progress_s OR when enough consecutive polls matched nothing that the screen cannot be one this config knows — see _BLIND_LAP_CYCLES. Home visible means there is nothing to recover, so rejoin at start_state; otherwise escalate to the restart, because a screen we cannot identify has no close button we can aim at. FOREGROUND CHECK ADDED 2026-08-19: on_absent now asks whether the game still owns the screen before walking the probe chain. Every state in that chain matches a game screen, so a screen that is not the game defeats all of them at once — caught live 19:01-19:11 when LDPlayer's own store (com.android.ld.appstore) opened over the running game: the bot jumped into a storefront for ten minutes, this recovery pass ran and could not help, and only the second watchdog fire would have cycled the app. require_foreground is a no-op when the game is in front, so the fire that recovers on its own (one of the two seen that day) still does.

recover_unknown_backspam_1._note: Fast BACK-press attempt before the expensive restart_app. Live 2026-08-21: a screen with no marker at all stalled a farm config for the full no_progress_s window before it even started recovering. Errand configs like this one have no probe chain to fall back through — home or restart is the whole recovery — so this sits directly ahead of restart_app instead of ahead of a probe walk. Android BACK dismisses most dialogs without needing to know what they are (see key()'s own docstring, and this very config's exit_to_home chain, which already relies on exactly this to leave the Friends panel). Bounded at 3 like exit_to_home, because BACK on home itself raises the game's own "Exit the game?" confirm.

recover_unknown_backspam_2._note: BACK press 2/3 of the fast-close attempt — see recover_unknown_backspam_1's note.

recover_unknown_backspam_3._note: BACK press 3/3 of the fast-close attempt — see recover_unknown_backspam_1's note.

recover_unknown_restart._note:
Expensive half, and the one that always works. A screen with no marker has no button to aim at, so cycle the process instead: restart_app -> recover_login re-auths -> start_state. An errand loses nothing by restarting — unlike the farm loop it has no run in flight to forfeit.
